facts.statement: The holotype skeleton was likely collected in the Linglongta area of Jianchang from the Tiaojishan Formation.

facts.statement: Xiaotingia was first named and classified by Xing Xu, Hailu You, Kai Du, and Fenglu Han in 2011.
facts.quote: Xiaotingia fue nombrado y clasificado inicialmente por Xing Xu, Hailu You, Kai Du y Fenglu Han en 2011

facts.statement: The type species, Xiaotingia zhengi, honors the paleontologist Zheng Xiaoting.

facts.statement: Xiaotingia lived in western Liaoning, China, during the Middle Jurassic or early Late Jurassic.
facts.quote: from Middle Jurassic or early Late Jurassic deposits of western Liaoning, China.

facts.statement: The animal lived between approximately 165 and 153 million years ago, spanning the Bathonian and Oxfordian stages.
facts.quote: vivió desde mediados a finales del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente entre 165 a 153 millones de años entre el Bathoniense y el Oxfordiense

facts.statement: According to the Paleobiology Database, the time range extends from the Bathonian to the Kimmeridgian (168.2 to 152.21 million years ago).

facts.statement: The dinosaur measured about 60 centimeters in length and weighed approximately 0.82 kilograms.

facts.statement: It had feathers on the head, body, forelimbs, and hind limbs.
facts.quote: Xiaotingia tenía plumas en la cabeza, el cuerpo, las extremidades anteriores y posteriores.

facts.statement: If it could fly short distances, it might have also used its hind limbs as wings.

facts.statement: It is classified within the family Anchiornithidae.

facts.statement: It is a genus of theropod ceratosaurian dinosaur.

facts.statement: A later analysis challenged the initial hypothesis, recovering Archaeopteryx as an avialan while placing Xiaotingia closely allied to Anchiornis within the Troodontidae.
facts.quote: This phylogenetic hypothesis was challenged by an analysis using different methods published several months later however, in which Archaeopteryx was again recovered as an avialan, while Xiaotingia remained closely allied to Anchiornis within the Troodontidae.

facts.statement: However, a more exhaustive analysis published months later questioned this, finding Archaeopteryx as an avialan again while Xiaotingia remained closely related to Anchiornis within Troodontidae.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, esto fue cuestionado por un análisis más exhaustivo publicado varios meses después, en el cual Archaeopteryx fue de nuevo encontrado como un avialano, mientras que Xiaotingia permanece cercanamente relacionado con Anchiornis dentro de Troodontidae.

facts.statement: However, in 2012 new revisions suggested Xiaotingia was a basal dromaeosaurid, not a troodontid.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, en 2012 nuevas revisiones sugirieron que Xiaotingia era un dromeosáurido basal, y no un troodóntido

facts.statement: A 2017 study re-examining the 'Harlem specimen' of Archaeopteryx concluded that Xiaotingia would belong to another family, the anchiornithids.
